subject: Vector Bridge — data residency & SLA terms
messages:
From: Kaitlyn Park <kaitlyn@pinecone.io>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Pinecone Solutions <solutions@pinecone.io>
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Vector Bridge pilot — residency & SLA overview

Hi Rishi,

Great to meet last week — thanks for the time. As discussed, I wanted to put together a short note that outlines the pilot scope for the Vector Bridge integration and call out the two items your team flagged: data residency (US vs EU) and an SLA for indexing/lookup latency.

Quick bullets:
- Pilot scope: 3-week PoC, up to 50M vectors, hybrid routing between Pinecone managed index and S3 cold tier.
- Data residency: Pinecone can ensure active index data resides in a single region (us-west-2) for the duration of the pilot. If you require an S3-only cold copy to remain in your VPC, we can provide an export hook.
- SLA ask: We can offer 99.9% availability for query endpoints under the dedicated pilot configuration; 99.5% is the default for shared clusters. Detailed latency SLOs depend on replication and provisioning — typical p95 query latencies are ~20–60ms for the vector sizes you described.
- Commercials: pilot is complimentary; if you convert to production we’ll propose a committed tier (TBD).

Attached: condensed SOC2 summary and our standard pilot checklist.

Next steps: can you confirm a) whether us-west-2 residency satisfies Redwood’s requirements and b) whether you want Pinecone to host the warm index or for Redwood to host warm + use Pinecone for similarity compute? We’ll loop legal once you confirm residency preference so we can prepare a short commercial/DSA addendum.

Thanks — happy to jump on a 30m call if helpful.

—Kaitlyn
Kaitlyn Park
Partnerships, Pinecone

Attachment: SOC2-summary.pdf (1 page summary)
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Kaitlyn Park <kaitlyn@pinecone.io>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Vector Bridge pilot — residency & SLA overview

Kaitlyn — thanks, this is helpful. Short answers up front:

1) Residency: us-west-2 is fine for the pilot, but production will require an option for EU-resident indexes for EU customers. We need the contract language to allow per-account regional pinning.
2) Hosting model: prefer Redwood to host the warm index in our Dedicated pool for predictable latency, with Pinecone handling the similarity compute (i.e., compute node adjacency) for scale. We want the ability to fail over to S3 cold tier within the same region without cross-region replication.

Laura and Aditya — looping you in for legal and integration constraints. Laura, if we go with Redwood-hosted warm index + Pinecone compute, what guardrails do we need around data processing and contract language to satisfy data sovereignty and auditability? Aditya — can you confirm that Redwood’s Dedicated runtime can export a consistent snapshot that Pinecone can ingest for the pilot and how long a snapshot takes for ~50M 1536-dim vectors?

Proposed next step: Laura to share redlines to your standard pilot addendum and Kaitlyn/Pinecone legal to return an updated short-form addendum. I’ll also schedule a short kickoff to lock down technical handoffs.

Thanks,
Rishi
Director, Partnerships — Redwood Inference
From: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Kaitlyn Park <kaitlyn@pinecone.io>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Pinecone Legal <legal@pinecone.io>
Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Vector Bridge pilot — residency & SLA overview

On Thu, Jun 11, 2026 at 10:03 AM Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com> wrote:
> Kaitlyn — thanks, this is helpful. Short answers up front:
>
> 1) Residency: us-west-2 is fine for the pilot, but production will require an option for EU-resident indexes for EU customers. We need the contract language to allow per-account regional pinning.
> 2) Hosting model: prefer Redwood to host the warm index in our Dedicated pool for predictable latency, with Pinecone handling the similarity compute (i.e., compute node adjacency) for scale. We want the ability to fail over to S3 cold tier within the same region without cross-region replication.

Kaitlyn — looping in Pinecone Legal as requested. A couple of legal/commercial items we’ll need addressed in the pilot addendum (we’ve attached a redline):

- Data processing: statement that Pinecone will act as a processor only for vectors they operate on for compute; Redwood remains data controller.
- Residency language: per-account regional pinning with export hooks and no automatic cross-region replication unless explicitly requested.
- Subprocessors: list of subprocessors used by Pinecone for the pilot; requirement for advance notice and opt-out for high-risk subprocessors.
- SLA: for the pilot, acceptable to document the availability/latency targets as non-contractual objectives but include a path to 99.9% contractual SLA upon conversion to a committed production tier.
- Liability & indemnities: cap aligned to the pilot value; we’ll revisit for production.

Please see attached: contract_redlines.pdf (two pages of brief redlines + comments). Aditya — please add a short note inline about snapshot cadence & expected snapshot size so Pinecone can confirm ingest window.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Attachment: contract_redlines.pdf
From: Pinecone Legal <legal@pinecone.io>
To: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Kaitlyn Park <kaitlyn@pinecone.io>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Vector Bridge pilot — residency & SLA overview

Laura / Rishi — thanks for the redlines and the clear framing. We reviewed the document and can accept the pilot-level constraints with small clarifications:

1) Processor/controller: we’re comfortable recognizing Redwood as the controller and Pinecone as a processor for the pilot. We will add a short DPA clause reflecting that and include Pinecone subprocessors.
2) Residency & export hooks: we confirm we can pin active indexes to us-west-2 for the pilot and provide an S3 export hook into your VPC in the same region. We will not enable cross-region replication without written consent.
3) SLA: we will include the pilot targets as "Service Objectives" and add a path to a contractual 99.9% SLA with commensurate pricing for committed capacity.

Next steps: we will prepare a revised pilot addendum that accepts your redlines (minor language edits only) and circulate for signature. Kaitlyn will follow up with a DocuSign link.
